questions.question: How are sorted document IDs converted to gaps?
options: Keep the first ID, then subtract each preceding ID from the current ID
Subtract every document ID from the final document ID
Store the difference between each ID and the vocabulary size
Replace every ID with its term frequency

questions.question: How are gap-encoded document IDs decoded?
options: By sorting each gap in descending order
By multiplying every gap by the term frequency
By computing cumulative prefix sums
By hashing each gap into a document bucket

questions.question: Why do frequent terms often require fewer bits per posting?
options: Their document IDs are stored without any order
They have no document IDs in their postings
Their absolute document IDs are always smaller than rare terms
Dense occurrence across documents tends to produce small gaps

questions.question: Why do compressed blocks store an absolute base or last document ID?
options: It provides a restart point for decoding or skipping into delta data
It makes every following gap equal to zero
It removes the need to preserve sorted document order
It converts positions into source character offsets

questions.question: Why can random external document IDs hurt gap compression?
options: They guarantee every term posting is locally dense
They destroy locality that could create small consecutive differences
They make document IDs strictly increasing within each list
They reduce every ID to a seven-bit integer

A byte offset may be mid-integer and prior gaps determine absolute IDs

Reverse the continuation convention automatically
